verdict.rationale: Proa's own repo documents built-in signals for interactive islands (proa-gh-3), and each island ships with seed state on a shared runtime (proa-docs-16), so it has first-party reactive state primitives. WebContext adds typed request-scoped and route state for server renders (proa-docs-18). These are framework-integrated primitives rather than a distinct, documented state management library, and the evidence is a single thin mention. Missing for 10: a dedicated official state management library or package, docs on its API (stores, cross-island or global state sharing), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
